scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Jungle, emphasizing the first English sequel expansion, the 64-row holo/non-holo mirror, Eeveelution forest memory, no-symbol error caution, and collector-facing identification rails.

sources.title: Pokemon TCG API v2 set record: Jungle

claims.text: The local catalog, Pokemon TCG API, and Bulbapedia model English Jungle as released on June 16, 1999.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API support a 64-row English Jungle checklist.
Bulbapedia describes Jungle as the second main expansion of the Pokemon Trading Card Game, with the English release expanded to 64 cards by including non-holofoil prints of the rare holo cards.

The local catalog preserves Jungle as Pokemon TCG API set id base2 and release_family_id en_wotc_jungle_19990616, separate from Japanese Pokemon Jungle, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, promo variants, and physical edition/error states.

Bulbapedia's error-card page records English Jungle no-symbol errors as an Unlimited Jungle holo-rare print issue; this supports a special identification rail but does not authenticate any individual card.

Bulbapedia lists additional Jungle-related promo or special rows such as Prerelease Clefable, gold-border Meowth, and W Promo Pikachu; those are adjacent branches, not automatic matches for ordinary Jungle catalog rows.

The local Jungle artist clusters are: Kagemaru Himeno (23 local rows; examples: Flareon, Jolteon, Pidgeot), Mitsuhiro Arita (19 local rows; examples: Clefable, Electrode, Kangaskhan), Ken Sugimori (17 local rows; examples: Mr. Mime, Nidoqueen, Scyther), Keiji Kinebuchi (5 local rows; examples: Vileplume, Vileplume, Gloom).

Jungle matters because it is the first English sequel expansion: Pokemon leaves the launch-room grammar and steps into a wilder collector space where Eeveelutions, Snorlax, Scyther, Pikachu, and the first big English error folklore make the set feel less like a rulebook and more like a binder page people wanted to live in.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent memory says Jungle, base2, no symbol, no set symbol, 1st Edition, Unlimited, holo, non-holo, Eeveelution, Scyther, Snorlax, Pikachu, Prerelease Clefable, W Promo Pikachu, gold-border Meowth, Base Set 2, or Legendary Collection.
special_identification_instructions.summary: English Jungle is a 64-row set where holo rares 1-16 have non-holo rare mirrors 17-32, and no-symbol claims belong to Unlimited Jungle holo rares only unless another sourced branch is provided.
steps: Preserve release_family_id en_wotc_jungle_19990616 and Pokemon TCG API set id base2.
Before transaction logic, read the printed card number and rarity surface: 1-16 are holo-rare catalog rows, 17-32 are non-holo rare mirror rows, and 33-64 are uncommon/common rows.
For no-symbol claims, require a clear lower-right set-symbol scan and edition context; do not infer no-symbol status from the catalog row, card name, or missing symbol in a low-resolution image.

Do not promote Prerelease Clefable, W Promo Pikachu, gold-border Meowth, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, Japanese Pokemon Jungle, First Edition, or Unlimited status without branch-specific evidence.
For price, condition, edition, error, or authenticity claims, use seller evidence, market evidence, and/or verifier judgment; this catalog only makes the identification questions legible.

narrative.human_title: The forest where the binder opens
narrative.why_it_matters: Jungle is where the English game stops feeling like only a launch apparatus and starts feeling like a place. The first set taught the grammar; Jungle gives the binder a habitat: Eevee splitting into Flareon, Jolteon, and Vaporeon, Snorlax blocking the path, Scyther flashing through the grass, Pikachu tucked among commons, and a whole folklore of set-symbol and print errors waiting at the lower right. For the protocol, it is a beautiful troublemaker. Same name can mean holo or non-holo, ordinary or no-symbol, base2 or a later reprint. The card has to tell you which forest it came from.

claims.text: The local catalog identifies Jungle row base2-1 as Clefable.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API record Clefable base2-1 as Rare Holo.

Clefable is the first English Jungle row and immediately tells the collector this set is different: softer, stranger, more fairy-tale than launch combat. Arita gives it a moonlit kind of quiet, and the card also carries branch pressure because Clefable has prerelease and no-symbol-adjacent memory around it.
Clefable sits at the front of the holo run and is a common place where prerelease and no-symbol language can blur.
